{{Quote|The Stennes homeworld of Stennaros is a world pock-marked with artillery craters, and the scars of years of persecution.|Imperial sentientologist Obo Rin's findings on Stennaros being recorded in his ''Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy''|<ref name="Ss" />}}
'''Stennaros''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Stennaros system/Legends|Stennaros system]], within the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region's]] [[Har Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. The [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Near-Human]] [[Stennes]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and its [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], [[Changeling/Legends|shape-shifting]] [[Stennes Shifter/Legends|Stennes Shifter]] offshoots, [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] of both species' persecution led to Stennaros being pock-marked with [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] craters and otherwise scarred. With prejudices against the Stennes Shifters leading to many members of both species being [[Death/Legends|killed]], the baseline Stennes were a closed [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] society, albeit being socially and culturally advanced within their own [[Star system/Legends|system]]. The Stennes further persecuted their Shifter offshoots, resulting in the latter being a homeless species not welcome on their own planet, with the considerably reduced Shifter population attempting to blend in or assimilate with their baseline species.

==Description==
Stennaros was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Ss" /> located in the [[Stennaros system/Legends|Stennaros system]], within the [[Har Worlds]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
{{Quote|As civilization spread through the Stennes sector, we either became prized commodities, or hunted. That is the way with humans, near or otherwise. But we are not easy prey. How can you hunt what you cannot see? Or rather, how can you hunt what you cannot help but not see?|Trinto Duaba talking about his species' history of persecution within their planet's sector|<ref name="Ss" />}}
Stennaros was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Near-Human]] [[Stennes]] [[Species/Legends|species]] along with their [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Changeling/Legends|shape-shifting]] offshoot, the [[Stennes Shifter/Legends|Stennes Shifters]]. The planet in [[Time/Legends|time]] became pock-marked with [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] craters and scarred from [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of persecution against its inhabitants.<ref name="Ss" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|These are more closely related to humanity than some of the more bigoted members would like to find out.|Obo Rin discussing the Near-Human nature of certain shape-shifting species, including Stennaros's Stennes Shifters|<ref name="Ss" />}}
[[File:TrintoDuaba-Promo.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Trinto Duaba was a Stennes Shifter, a species native to Stennaros.]]
The Stennes and Stennes Shifters were native to Stennaros. With the Stennes Shifters being subject to other species' fear and prejudice, [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] of persecution led to many of the baseline Stennes being [[Death/Legends|killed]]. At one point, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], who had recognized the Stennes Shifters being a threat, fought the species and killed enough to significantly reduce its population. As a result of persecution affecting both them and their Shifter offshoots, the baseline Stennes were [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] and avoided contact with the outside world, although they were socially and culturally advanced within their own closed [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="Ss" />

Baseline Stennes further persecuted their Shifter offshoots, resulting in the latter becoming a homeless species not even welcome on its own homeworld. The few remaining Shifters would avoid exposing themselves, posing as normal Stennes and only using their powers when necessary. The Shifters who could not assimilate would blend into crowds and work as [[Thief/Legends|thieves]], [[Spy/Legends|spies]], or [[Information broker/Legends|informants]].<ref name="Ss" />

At a certain point, the Stennes Shifter [[Trinto Duaba/Legends|Trinto Duaba]] discussed<ref name="Ss" /> his<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|pack=#37: Trinto Duaba & Dice Ibegon|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLC37trintodice.asp}}</ref> species and its homeworld with [[Shi'ido]] [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Vandolae]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], around five thousand years after the Jedi Knights' attack on the Stennes Shifter species, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[sentientologist]] [[Obo Rin]] obtained the information about Stennaros and its Stennes and Stennes Shifter species from Vandolae, which Rin published in his ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]''.<ref name="Ss" />

==Behind the scenes==
Stennaros was introduced in the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]] source article "[[Shape-shifters]]," written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] for [[February]] [[1997]]'s [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 12|twelfth issue]] of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine.<ref name="Ss" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Stennaros system, and therefore Stennaros, in grid square K-16.<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Although "Shape-shifters" placed Stennaros in the "Stennes sector,"<ref name="Ss" /> [[Jason Fry]], co-author of ''The Essential Atlas'', later stated that [[Lucasfilm]] had requested the omission of that name from the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to ''The Essential Atlas'' in order to avoid confusion with the [[Stenness Node]],<ref name="Email">{{EmailCite|email=File:EAOC discussion.jpg|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2015-06-30}}</ref> a group of [[Mining/Legends|mining]] [[Star/Legends|star]] systems.<ref name="TotJ4">[[Tales of the Jedi 4|''Tales of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref> Instead, the Online Companion placed the Stennaros system, and therefore Stennaros, in the Har Worlds sector.<ref name="EAOC" />
